slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you better at
your job without working longer
Clarify the goal before you start. "What does a great result look like here?" Five minutes of questions saves days of work on the wrong thing.
Turn off notifications for deep work blocks. Ninety minutes with no emails or messages often produces far more than a whole scattered afternoon of jumping between tasks.
Keep a running list of what you've learned. Mistakes, shortcuts, good templates. Next time, you don't start from zero, you start from your notes.
Ask for feedback early, not at the end. Showing a rough draft on day two catches problems while they're still small and easy to fix.
Before: tired by noon, ideas all the same. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and fresh examples from other fields that sharpen my work.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: tired by noon, same old ideas. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Fresh examples from other fields sharpen my work.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn the shortcuts of the tools you use every day. Keyboard shortcuts, templates, filters. Small savings repeated a hundred times become hours.
Leave on time and rest properly. Tired people make slow decisions and silly mistakes. Real rest is part of doing the job well, not the opposite.
